'''Iraj Lalezari''' (1930–2019) was an Iranian academic. His study fields were [[organic chemistry]] and [[pharmacology]]. He left Iran in 1979 following the [[Iranian Revolution|regime change]] in the country and settled in the US where he continued his academic studies.

==Early life and education==
Lalezari was born in [[Hamadan]] on 4 July 1930.<ref name=7dor>{{cite web|title=Iraj Lalezari|date=7 November 2021|access-date=28 January 2023 |url=https://www.7dorim.com/en/nobility/iraj-lalezari/|publisher=7dorim}}</ref><ref name=evita>{{cite web|title=Dr. Iraj Lalezari
|publisher=echovita|access-date=28 January 2023|url=https://www.echovita.com/us/obituaries/co/louisville/iraj-lalezari-9513578}}</ref> He was the eldest of four siblings.<ref name=karm/> He received a degree in pharmacology from the [[University of Tehran]].<ref name=7dor/> He obtained his PhD in pharmacology from his alma mater in 1951.<ref name=gsfla>{{cite web|title=Biographical Sketch. Iraj Lalezari|access-date=28 January 2023 |url=http://thegraduatesocietyla.org/Lalehzari%20Biographi-English.html|publisher=Graduate Society Foundation}}</ref> He also received a PhD in organic chemistry from the [[University of Paris|University of Sorbonne]] in 1953.<ref name=7dor/><ref name=gsfla/> He carried out his post-doctorate studies in organic chemistry at the same institution in 1954.<ref name=gsfla/>

==Career and activities==
Following his graduation, Lalezari joined the University of Tehran where he served as the chair of the chemistry department (1970–1978) and the dean of the pharmacology faculty (1973–1979).<ref name=karm/> In 1964 he was promoted to a professorship in organic chemistry.<ref name=gsfla/> He was named as the chair of the Iranian Pharmaceutical Association in 1975 which he held until 1979.<ref name=gsfla/> In 1976 he was made a member of the Iranian Royal Academy of Sciences.<ref name=gsfla/> In 1977 he established the Institute at Medicinal Plants at the University of Tehran which he headed until 1979.<ref name=gsfla/>

He had to leave Iran due to the establishment of an Islamic government in February 1979 and continued his academic studies in New York City<ref name=karm/> where he worked at the [[Montefiore Medical Center]] and [[Albert Einstein College of Medicine]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Iraj Lalezari|title=One-step synthesis of 3-amino-2,4-imidazolinediones (3-aminohydantoins) from α-amino acids|journal=[[Journal of Heterocyclic Chemistry]]|date=May–June 1985|volume=22|issue=3|pages=741–743|doi=10.1002/jhet.5570220325}}</ref> He served as the director of medicinal chemistry in the latter.<ref name=cellv>{{cite web|title=Our Story|date=24 January 2019 |url=https://cellviable.com/our-story/|publisher=Cell Viable|access-date=28 January 2023}}</ref>

Lalezari was part of the Iranian Jewish delegation led by [[Moussa Kermanian]] who met with [[President of the United States|President]] [[Jimmy Carter]] in 1980.<ref name=karm/> The goal of the meeting was to facilitate the migration of Iranian Jews to the US.<ref name=karm/>

He was a member of the American Jewish Federation and the Maccabee Foundation based in New York.<ref>{{cite web|title=About The Maccabee Foundation|url=http://maccabeefoundation.org/about-us/|publisher=Maccabee Foundation|access-date=28 January 2023}}</ref> In 2006 Lalezari retired from academic life.<ref name=karm/>

===Patents and work===
Lalezari had numerous [[Patent|patents]] which he obtained between February 1977 and May 2015, including treatments for [[Alzheimer's disease]] using [[gene therapy]] methodologies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patents by Inventor Iraj Lalezari|publisher=Justia Patents|access-date=28 January 2023|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/iraj-lalezari}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patent summary. Novel inhibitors of formation of advanced glycation endproducts (ages)|url=https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/patent/WO-02072083-A1|publisher=[[United States National Library of Medicine]]
|access-date=28 January 2023}}</ref> Some of these patents were taken jointly by him and his brother Parviz.<ref>{{cite web|title=Method of synthesis and novel compounds for pharmaceutical uses (WO1989012622A1)|publisher=Google patents|access-date=28 January 2023
|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/WO1989012622A1/en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Official Gazette of the United States Patent and Trademark Office: Patents|publisher=U.S. Department of Commerce, Patent and Trademark Office|issue=1235|year=2000|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1g16MQTtlIcC&pg=RA1-PA581|page=1-PA581|location=Washington, DC}}</ref> 

Iraj Lalezari discovered the [[Glycated hemoglobin|hemoglobin A1C]] test which has been used in many countries to diagnose [[diabetes]].<ref name=karm/> He also invented some compounds of [[fluoride]] and [[selenium]].<ref name=karm/>

==Later years, personal life and death==
Lalezari was married and had two sons.<ref name=7dor/> Following his retirement he settled in Colorado and continued his studies at his home laboratory.<ref name=karm/> In 2010 he joined Cell Viable, a company that develops and produces skincare products.<ref name=cellv/> He died in [[Boulder, Colorado]], on 31 July 2019.<ref name=evita/><ref name=karm>{{cite news|author=Karmel Melamed|title=Iranian Jews mourn passing of scientific giant Dr. Iraj Lalezari|access-date=28 January 2023|work=[[Jewish News Syndicate]]|url=https://www.jns.org/opinion/iranian-jews-mourn-passing-of-scientific-giant-dr-iraj-lalezari/}}</ref> He was buried at the Green Mountain Cemetery in Boulder on 2 August.<ref>{{cite web
|title=Dr. Iraj Lalezari. 1930 - 2019|url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/legacy/obituary.aspx?n=iraj-lalezari&pid=193532195&fhid=6730
|publisher=Legacy|access-date=28 January 2023}}</ref>

==Awards==
Lalezari was the recipient of the [[Lavoisier Medal]] which was granted to him in 1954 by the [[Société chimique de France|French Chemical Society]].<ref name=karm/><ref name=gsfla/> He was also awarded by the Shah [[Mohammad Reza Pahlavi]] and Empress [[Farah Pahlavi]] for his outstanding studies.<ref name=karm/><ref name=gsfla/>
